rules.title: Newark application fee cap (Ch. 19:6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge more than $25 per adult applicant as an application fee. The landlord must give a written receipt and, within 14 days after the application is denied or withdrawn, refund any part of the fee not spent on a credit or background check.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any landlord in Newark charging application fees.
rules.interaction: New local rule; sets a lower cap than the NJ state $50 cap (P.L.2025, c.405) without amending any existing Newark rule.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall charge an application fee exceeding twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per adult applicant
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation; enforced by the Department of Economic and Housing Development.
rules.effective_date_note: Section 19:6-7 states the ordinance takes effect January 1, 2027 (after the 2026-10-01 query date).
rules.prior_version_note: No earlier Newark application fee cap is stated; this is a new chapter.

in_force_since_evidence.quoted_span: This ordinance shall take effect on January 1, 2027

rules.source_type: official (text supplied on the Try it page)
rules.review_note: The document labels itself a fictional sample ordinance and not a law of the City of Newark. The 5+ unit limit and Housing Authority exemption in § 19:6-3 apply only to § 19:6-2, not to the fee cap.

rules.title: Newark ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Ch. 19:6)
rules.requirement: Landlords of buildings with five or more units may not use software that uses nonpublic rent, occupancy or lease data from two or more landlords to recommend or set rents. Selling, licensing or providing such a device for that purpose is also barred; reports of aggregated data that do not recommend rents for specific units are allowed.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic multi-landlord data (5+ unit buildings)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords of buildings with 5 or more dwelling units in Newark.
rules.exemptions: Buildings with four or fewer dwelling units; units owned and operated by the Newark Housing Authority; reports of aggregated rent data that do not recommend rents for specific units.
rules.interaction: Adds a new local rule; does not amend or replace an existing Newark rule. NJ's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) covers the same subject at the state level.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord of a building containing five or more dwelling units shall use an algorithmic rent-setting device to
set the rent for any dwelling unit in the City, and no person shall sell, license or provide such a device for that
purpose
rules.conflict_note: NJ's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) may interact with or preempt local algorithmic rent-setting rules once effective. State rule NJ-ALG-01 (P.L.2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once effective (2027-07-01).

unverifiable_exemptions: unit owned and operated by the Newark Housing Authority

rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation; each month of use for a dwelling unit is a separate violation; enforced by the Department of Economic and Housing Development.
rules.effective_date_note: Section 19:6-7 states the ordinance takes effect January 1, 2027 (after the 2026-10-01 query date).
rules.prior_version_note: No earlier Newark rule of this kind is stated; this is a new chapter.

in_force_since_evidence.quoted_span: This ordinance shall take effect on January 1, 2027

NWK-FEE-01.question_en: What can be charged to apply or move in?
NWK-FEE-01.question_es: ¿Qué se puede cobrar por solicitar o al mudarse?
NWK-FEE-01.why_en: Landlords must give a receipt and refund unused fees within 14 days if denied or withdrawn.
NWK-FEE-01.answer_es: Desde el 1 ene 2027: máximo $25 por solicitar.
NWK-FEE-01.why_es: El propietario debe dar recibo y devolver lo no gastado en 14 días si se niega o se retira.

NWK-ALG-01.question_en: Can software be used to set the rent?
NWK-ALG-01.question_es: ¿Se puede usar software para fijar la renta?
NWK-ALG-01.answer_en: From Jan 1, 2027: not with secret shared data.
NWK-ALG-01.why_en: It applies to buildings with 5 or more units, when software uses nonpublic data from 2 or more landlords.
NWK-ALG-01.answer_es: Desde el 1 ene 2027: no con datos privados compartidos.
NWK-ALG-01.why_es: Rige en edificios con 5 o más unidades, si el software usa datos no públicos de 2 o más propietarios.

rules.title: Newark application fee cap (Ch. 19:6)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not charge more than $25 per adult applicant as an application fee. The landlord must give a written receipt and, within 14 days after the application is denied or withdrawn, refund any part of the fee not spent on a credit or background check.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any landlord in Newark charging application fees.
rules.interaction: New local rule; sets a lower cap than the NJ state $50 cap (P.L.2025, c.405) without amending any existing Newark rule.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall charge an application fee exceeding twenty-five dollars ($25.00) per adult applicant
rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation; enforced by the Department of Economic and Housing Development.
rules.effective_date_note: Section 19:6-7 states the ordinance takes effect January 1, 2027 (after the 2026-10-01 query date).
rules.prior_version_note: No earlier Newark application fee cap is stated; this is a new chapter.

in_force_since_evidence.quoted_span: This ordinance shall take effect on January 1, 2027

rules.source_type: official (text supplied on the Try it page)
rules.review_note: The document labels itself a fictional sample ordinance and not a law of the City of Newark. The 5+ unit limit and Housing Authority exemption in § 19:6-3 apply only to § 19:6-2, not to the fee cap.

rules.title: Newark ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Ch. 19:6)
rules.requirement: Landlords of buildings with five or more units may not use software that uses nonpublic rent, occupancy or lease data from two or more landlords to recommend or set rents. Selling, licensing or providing such a device for that purpose is also barred; reports of aggregated data that do not recommend rents for specific units are allowed.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic multi-landlord data (5+ unit buildings)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords of buildings with 5 or more dwelling units in Newark.
rules.exemptions: Buildings with four or fewer dwelling units; units owned and operated by the Newark Housing Authority; reports of aggregated rent data that do not recommend rents for specific units.
rules.interaction: Adds a new local rule; does not amend or replace an existing Newark rule. NJ's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) covers the same subject at the state level.
rules.quoted_span:
No landlord of a building containing five or more dwelling units shall use an algorithmic rent-setting device to
set the rent for any dwelling unit in the City, and no person shall sell, license or provide such a device for that
purpose
rules.conflict_note: NJ's FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) may interact with or preempt local algorithmic rent-setting rules once effective. State rule NJ-ALG-01 (P.L.2026, c.43) may preempt this ordinance once effective (2027-07-01).

rules.penalty: Civil penalty up to $2,000 per violation; each month of use for a dwelling unit is a separate violation; enforced by the Department of Economic and Housing Development.
